items.title: Al Udeid Air Base, Qatar, Qatar: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif arrived in Doha to offer condolences to Qatar's Emir over the death of former Emir Hamad bin Khalifa al Thani.
items.description: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif arrived in Doha to offer condolences to Qatar's Emir over the death of former Emir Hamad bin Khalifa al Thani.
items.rawSummary: Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar faces sustained Iranian missile attacks amid high-level diplomatic maneuvering, the death of a former emir, and new condolences visits from regional allies.
items.analysis: Qatar is simultaneously a center of intense mediation and the target of escalating Iranian strikes, a volatile context deepened by the death of former Emir Hamad bin Khalifa al Thani. Diplomatic efforts continue: the prime minister spoke with Iran's foreign minister, and Qatar and Pakistan are spearheading efforts to bring the United States and Iran back to negotiations, with a four-way call involving the U.S., Pakistan, Qatar, and Iran planned. In a further sign of regional solidarity, Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif arrived in Doha to offer condolences to the Amir. Hours after strikes on Qatar wounded several people, Iranian President Pezeshkian sent condolences over the former emir's death, while Qatar itself called for an immediate halt to the fighting and a return to dialogue. The funeral of the former emir was held in Doha, with his son and current Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al Thani carrying the body. Economic consequences are growing as Qatar paused its LNG production push after an attack on a tanker, and its sovereign wealth fund blocked a Volkswagen deal with Israel's Rafael, prompting Israel to halt a shipping agreement. Satellite imagery confirmed direct hits on a hangar at Al Udeid airbase and on the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain from Iranian missiles and drones, following multiple ballistic missile attacks that triggered air defense responses in Doha.

items.title: European Parliament, Brussels, Belgium: The European Union revealed that Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) was responsible for a series of malicious cyberattacks targeting governmental networks and critical infrastructure in EU member states and Ukraine.
items.description: The European Union revealed that Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) was responsible for a series of malicious cyberattacks targeting governmental networks and critical infrastructure in EU member states and Ukraine.
items.rawSummary: The European Union is confronting a range of security and economic challenges, from attributing cyberattacks to Russia’s FSB and boosting defense spending to reducing reliance on China and advancing support for Ukraine and Gaza.
items.analysis: Recent revelations of a January 2026 closed-door 'therapy night' exposed EU leaders' anxiety over U.S. reliability and fueled calls for strategic independence, while NATO Secretary General Rutte has stressed deepening Russia-China-North Korea-Iran cooperation and pushed defense spending toward 5% of GDP by 2035, with Europe already nearing 4%. Belgian Prime Minister De Wever highlighted a 60% defense spending increase and two €70 billion Ukraine support packages as an irreversible 'red card' for Moscow, and the EU authorized Ukraine to use a $69 billion loan for British arms purchases. The European Union also publicly attributed a series of malicious cyberattacks targeting governmental networks and critical infrastructure in multiple member states and Ukraine to Russia’s FSB, adding to the security tensions. On economic and regulatory fronts, the bloc is preparing a fund to reduce dependence on Chinese suppliers amid a €360 billion trade deficit, demanding that Meta redesign engagement features under threat of fines, and has launched a €883.6 million 'Team Gaza Initiative' while the Commission considered banning imports from Israeli settlements.

items.rawSummary: A fire in a Bangkok restaurant killed at least 29 people.
items.analysis: A fire swept through a restaurant in the Chom Phon area of Chatuchak district in Bangkok, causing at least 29 deaths. items.title: Tokyo, Japan: The New York Times reported that Japan is building its first centralized intelligence agency since World War II, with advice from the U.S., Australia, and Germany, to improve intelligence sharing, cybersecurity, and counterespionage against threats from China, Russia, and North Korea.
items.description: The New York Times reported that Japan is building its first centralized intelligence agency since World War II, with advice from the U.S., Australia, and Germany, to improve intelligence sharing, cybersecurity, and counterespionage against threats from China, Russia, and North Korea.
items.rawSummary: Japan's bond market experienced sharp swings amid signals of domestic pension fund reallocation and accelerating central bank asset reduction, while the government acknowledged Russian espionage threats and moved to create its first postwar centralized intelligence agency.
items.analysis: The Bank of Japan's balance sheet shrank by $146 billion in the second quarter to $3.97 trillion, the lowest since early 2020, as its quantitative tightening program drove JGB holdings down by $78 billion and trimmed equity ETF and J-REIT holdings. That week, the 10-year JGB yield experienced extreme swings, dropping 16 basis points to 2.71% on Friday after briefly touching 2.90% a day earlier, while the 30-year yield fell 13 basis points, partly on the Finance Minister's signal that the $1.8 trillion Government Pension Investment Fund should increase its domestic asset allocation, which could support the yen. In parallel, The Japan Times reported that Russian intelligence operatives have exploited weak counter-espionage laws to acquire advanced Japanese technology for weapons, a finding echoed by a New York Times report on July 13 that called the country a Russian "den of spies" and prompted Tokyo to say it needs stronger counterintelligence. The same day, the NYT reported that Japan is building its first centralized intelligence agency since World War II, with U.S., Australian, and German advice, aimed at improving intelligence sharing, cybersecurity, and counterespionage against regional threats.

items.title: United States, United States: US researchers announce the first complete robotic surgery on live animals using a humanoid robot, with the Chinese Unitree G1 performing gallbladder procedures on pigs.
items.description: US researchers announce the first complete robotic surgery on live animals using a humanoid robot, with the Chinese Unitree G1 performing gallbladder procedures on pigs.
items.rawSummary: US researchers achieve the first complete robotic surgery on live animals using a humanoid robot, with China's Unitree G1 performing gallbladder procedures on pigs.
items.analysis: A US research team successfully used China's Unitree G1 humanoid robot to perform minimally invasive gallbladder surgery on two live pigs, completing what is described as the world's first full robotic surgical procedure on live animals using a humanoid robot. The achievement highlights rapid progress in medical robotics and cross-border technology application, potentially pointing toward future surgical automation and expanded roles for humanoid robots in healthcare.

items.title: Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, United States: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is reportedly hesitant to travel to the U.S. for Senator Graham's funeral unless a formal meeting with President Trump is also arranged, N12 reports.
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is reportedly hesitant to travel to the U.S. for Senator Graham's funeral unless a formal meeting with President Trump is also arranged, N12 reports.
items.rawSummary: Following Senator Lindsey Graham's sudden death, President Trump underwent a scheduled physical at Walter Reed while the political and diplomatic fallout reverberates, including the medical examiner's findings, Trump's succession planning, Senator McConnell's health disclosure, and international reactions such as Iraqi Prime Minister al Zaidi's upcoming visit and Prime Minister Netanyahu's conditional travel for the funeral.
items.analysis: President Trump underwent a scheduled physical at Walter Reed while Washington absorbed the sudden death of Senator Graham, who collapsed hours after a phone call with Trump about Ukraine, Russia sanctions, and Iran. Axios reported that Graham felt unwell after the call but declined immediate medical attention and later died at a hospital from an aortic dissection caused by cardiovascular disease, with no indication of foul play. Trump said he has someone in mind to fill Graham's seat, while Senator McConnell disclosed his own recent hospitalization for a fall, brief unconsciousness, and pneumonia, and is now in rehabilitation. The diplomatic calendar remains active: Iraqi Prime Minister al Zaidi is due in Washington for oil and gas talks, and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is hesitant to attend Graham's funeral unless a formal meeting with Trump is arranged, N12 reports.

items.rawSummary: Vessel approached by six boats south of Aden; security team fires warning shots
items.analysis: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre issued an advisory after a commercial vessel 50 nautical miles south of Aden reported being approached by six small boats. The ship’s security team fired warning shots and the boats were trailing one nautical mile behind. The incident underscores persistent risks to commercial shipping in the Gulf of Aden and waters off Yemen, where Houthi-related threats have been elevated for months.

items.rawSummary: Merchant tanker approached by small boats off Aden; warning shots fired
items.analysis: The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a tanker transiting east in the Internationally Recommended Transit Corridor was approached by six small boats from the starboard side. One boat closed to within 5 cables, prompting the onboard armed security team to fire warning shots, while the remaining five stayed at 1 nautical mile. No boarding or damage has been reported, and authorities are investigating. The approach occurred 50 nautical miles south of Aden in a corridor that has seen repeated suspicious approaches and Houthi-linked threats.

Trump said he has someone in mind to fill Graham's seat, while Senator McConnell disclosed his own recent hospitalization for a fall, brief unconsciousness, and pneumonia, and is now in rehabilitation. The diplomatic calendar remains active: Iraqi Prime Minister al Zaidi is due in Washington for oil and gas talks, and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is hesitant to attend Graham's funeral unless a formal meeting with Trump is arranged, N12 reports.
items.locationName: Walter Reed National Military Medical Center
items.keyPoint: Axios reported that in his final hours, Senator Graham called President Trump to brief on his Ukraine trip, press for a Senate vote on new Russia sanctions, and joked he 'can't die now,' citing unfinished business including Russia sanctions, Iran, and Israeli-Saudi normalization, while Trump said he was preparing fresh strikes on Iran.
